claim: useFieldArray API surface (append/prepend/insert/swap/move/update/replace/remove) and its hard rules: field.id as key, no flat field arrays, shouldUnregister:true unsupported, append requires full defaults, don't stack actions.
quote: The field.id (and not index) must be added as the component key to prevent re-renders breaking the fields... Does not support flat field array... shouldUnregister: true is not supported. Field array relies on inputs being mounted and unmounted to manage its internal state — enabling shouldUnregister causes newly added fields to be unregistered on re-render, so their values are lost.

claim: Nested field arrays require one useFieldArray per level keyed on the parent index; parent remove/swap/move propagate to nested arrays via control._subjects.array; shouldUnregister governs whether unmounted array data survives.
quote: The control object's `_subjects.array` notifies all subscribed instances when the parent structure changes.

claim: register supports a `deps` option that triggers validation of dependent inputs; only dot path syntax is supported; shouldUnregister should be avoided with useFieldArray.
quote: deps | string | string[] | Validation will be triggered for the dependent inputs, it only limited to register api not trigger. ... Note: this prop should be avoided when using with useFieldArray as unregister function gets called after input unmount/remount and reorder. ... register("test.0.firstName") // ✅  register("test[0].firstName") // ❌

claim: RHF v8 beta adds first-class React Compiler support and flat field arrays; renames field id to key, removes keyName, removes the watch callback API in favour of subscribe, and stops setValue from updating field arrays (use replace).
quote: V8 adds first-class support for the React Compiler. No additional configuration is required... V8 supports flat field arrays... The internal render identifier has been renamed from id to key... setValue no longer directly updates useFieldArray fields. Use the replace method from useFieldArray instead.

claim: RHF's subscribe() lets you observe formState and values without triggering a render, and is the replacement for the watch callback.
quote: Subscribe to formState changes and value updates. You can subscribe to individual fields or the entire form, while avoiding unnecessary re-renders caused by form changes. ... This function is dedicated for subscribe form state without render, use this function for that instead of watch callback function.

claim: RHF's official wizard recipe stores cross-step data in an external store (little-state-machine) with one useForm per route; FormProvider re-renders the subtree on state updates; virtualized lists need form-level defaultValues so rows restore on remount.
quote: We recommend using a state management library to store user input through different pages or sections. In this example, we are going to use little state machine... this will cause issues as the items are removed from the DOM when they are out of view and re-added. This will cause items to reset to their default values when they re-enter the viewport.

claim: RHF field arrays with 100+ fields go laggy when formState is subscribed at the root; maintainer attributes it to dirtyFields updates re-rendering the whole form, and recommends localized subscription, register over Controller, and virtualization past ~1000 fields.
quote: Changing a field updates different form states like `dirtyFields` state, which would cause your whole form to re-render due to that update subscription you made in the parent component.

claim: Community consensus for RHF async uniqueness checks: keep the remote check out of the Zod resolver; run it via useWatch + debounce + AbortController and surface it with setError/clearErrors.
quote: Keep Zod for sync validation... use `setError` / `clearErrors` for the remote result

claim: TanStack Form arrays use <form.Field mode="array">, field.pushValue(...) to append, bracket-indexed subfield names, and the official example keys rows by array index.
quote: <form.Field name="people" mode="array"> ... <button onClick={() => field.pushValue({ name: '', age: 0 })} type="button">Add person</button> ... <form.Field key={i} name={`people[${i}].name`}>

claim: TanStack Form has built-in async validation with per-field asyncDebounceMs, runs sync validators before async ones unless asyncAlways is set, supports form-level validators that write errors onto specific field paths, and accepts any Standard Schema library.
quote: asyncDebounceMs={500} ... The synchronous method runs first; the async method only runs if sync validation succeeds—unless you set asyncAlways to true. ... onSubmitAsync: async ({ value }) => { return { form: 'Invalid data', fields: { age: 'Must be 13 or older to sign', 'details.email': 'An email is required' } } }

claim: TanStack Form models cross-field dependencies declaratively with onChangeListenTo / onBlurListenTo, and warns that mutual listening creates infinite validation loops.
quote: When you specify onChangeListenTo: ['password'] on a field, the onChange validator runs both when that field itself changes and whenever the specified linked field changes.

claim: TanStack Form's re-render model is selector subscriptions: form.Subscribe isolates the re-render to the subscribing children, useSelector re-renders the whole component, and omitting the selector re-renders on every form state change; useStore is deprecated in favour of useSelector.
quote: form.Subscribe doesn't trigger component-level re-renders. Anytime the value subscribed to changes, only the form.Subscribe component re-renders ... Omitting selectors causes many unnecessary re-renders whenever any of the form state changes ... useStore is still exported but deprecated.

claim: TanStack Form's FormGroup / withFieldGroup gives each wizard step its own validators and an onGroupSubmit handler while the values stay in one parent form store.
quote: form groups can have their own validation ... a way to build out sub-forms that make this kind of development trivial to implement.

claim: form.Subscribe re-renders on every form mutation when the selector returns an object or array, because LocalSubscribe compares with Object.is and the selector allocates a fresh reference each time; open since Mar 2026, fix is to pass shallow equality.
quote: Since selectors that return objects/arrays create a new reference on every store update, the component re-renders every time any field in the form changes — not just the fields the selector cares about.

claim: Mounting/unmounting <form.Field> scales worse than linearly: ~1300 fields take 10+ seconds and can crash the tab, versus ~200ms for plain inputs (TanStack Form v1.29.1, May 2026).
quote: worse than O(N)—something like O(N^2) ... ~1,300 fields: 10+ seconds, occasionally crashes Chrome tabs ... Plain inputs: ~200ms

claim: Removing an item from a TanStack Form array inside a conditionally rendered form duplicates the last element ([1,2,3,4] minus item 2 yields [1,3,4,4]) because rows are reconciled by index.
quote: removing item 2 from [1, 2, 3, 4] results in [1, 3, 4, 4] instead of [1, 3, 4].

claim: Unmounting a TanStack Form field leaves its value, meta and fieldInfo in the form store; form.deleteField is the manual escape hatch.
quote: Unmounting a field preserves the state and fieldInfo of the field in the form even after unmounting it.

claim: A TanStack Form field that unmounts while holding a validation error keeps that error in the store and blocks submission.
quote: When a field is unmounted, it remains in the form including any errors, and if the field had validation errors they still persist and prevent the form from being submitted.

claim: Conform addresses nested data with object.property / array[index] name syntax, getFieldset() for objects and getFieldList() for arrays, with a per-item key from field metadata.
quote: Conform uses the `object.property` and `array[index]` syntax to denote data structure ... const tasks = fields.tasks.getFieldList(); tasks.map((task) => (<input name={task.name} />))

claim: Conform mutates field lists through submit-button intents (insert/remove/reorder/update/validate/reset) serialized into the form submitter, so array editing works without JavaScript.
quote: <button {...form.reorder.getButtonProps({ name: fields.tasks.name, from: index, to: 0 })}>Move to top</button>

claim: Conform's async-validation pattern builds the Zod schema from the submission intent: the client emits VALIDATION_SKIPPED for untargeted fields and VALIDATION_UNDEFINED when the async check is unavailable, which makes the server re-run it with parseWithZod({ async: true }).
quote: conformZodMessage.VALIDATION_UNDEFINED: This message is used to indicate that the validation is not defined and Conform should fallback to server validation.

claim: Conform can run the server schema on every input/blur, not just submit, via shouldValidate / shouldRevalidate, and deliberately has no client-side async validation — it falls back to the server instead of hitting a side endpoint.
quote: Instead of sending a request to another endpoint, we will simply fallback to server validation when needed.

claim: Because Conform reads values from the DOM, unmounted fields lose their values; PreserveBoundary re-injects them and is the sanctioned fix for multi-step wizards, dialogs and virtualized lists.
quote: A React component that preserves form field values during client-side navigation when React unmounts its contents.

claim: PreserveBoundary shipped in Conform v1.17.0; v1.19.4 (Jun 2026) patched a denial-of-service in the future parseSubmission API triggered by submissions with many repeated fields.
quote: Added PreserveBoundary component for preserving form values when fields are unmounted during client-side navigation ... v1.19.4: security patch addressed a denial-of-service vulnerability in the parseSubmission API from @conform-to/react/future, affecting submissions with numerous repeated fields.

claim: Bundle sizes measured May 2026 with esbuild: RHF ~9 kB core / ~14 kB with Zod; TanStack Form ~6 kB / ~11 kB; Formik ~13 kB / ~18 kB (min+gzip).
quote: Numbers below are minified + gzipped, measured against current versions in May 2026 with esbuild and a single useForm import.

claim: TanStack Form's own comparison table claims ✅ for built-in async debounce and granular per-field subscriptions where React Hook Form is ❓, and flags RHF nested field arrays as ✅*(1) — requiring TypeScript casts.
quote: Built-in Async Validation Debounce — TanStack Form: ✅, React Hook Form: ❓ ... Nested Arrays — React Hook Form: ✅*(1)

claim: RHF v7's mutable-ref + getter-based formState subscription is structurally incompatible with the React Compiler: memoization never invalidates, so watch() goes stale and errors stop updating; 'use no memo' is the v7 workaround.
quote: The design of React Hook Form itself conflicts with the assumptions of React Compiler. ... the subscription is never established, and `formState.errors` or `formState.isDirty` stop updating.

claim: Conform's useInputControl adapts custom/controlled widgets, but resets the value whenever the field key changes — which is exactly what insert/remove/reorder intents do.
quote: The only exception is if you are setting up a controlled input with the useInputControl hook which will reset the value when the key changes.

claim: React Hook Form star count and latest v7 release (7.81.0, Jul 5 2026).
TanStack Form star count and active v1.30.x release train (Jul 2026).
quote: 6.6k stars — @tanstack/preact-form@1.30.2, Jul 13, 2026

claim: Conform star count and latest release (1.19.4, Jun 2026).

Drag-and-drop over nested RHF field arrays breaks when a single ref holds the reorder function: appending a new nested array overwrites it and only the last array reorders; keep a list of reorder callbacks instead.
quote: When using the same ref for nested field arrays to store reorder functions, appending new nested child field arrays will override the reorder function and only move items belonging to the last nested field array.

claim: A common RHF wizard pattern gives each step its own useForm with defaultValues seeded from a React context store, and defers cross-step validation to a final confirmation step.
quote: Remove field validation for each step, and instead, display the state of each step in the Stepper.

claim: The community-standard RHF per-step gate is a per-step schema object plus await trigger(fieldNames) before advancing, with shouldUnregister:false keeping values across steps.
quote: We use an object of validations for each step and then trigger that specific object explicitly.
